finalSummary:
Done. The implementation is complete and all tests pass. Here's what was delivered:

**Pagination**: The `/products` endpoint now supports cursor-based pagination by default (`?limit=X&cursor=Y`), with an option to switch to offset paging (`?offset=N&limit=X`). Cursor pagination prevents skipped/duplicate rows if data changes between requests.

**Rate limiting**: Per-IP rate limiting is active with a 60-request burst capacity and 1 request/second sustained rate (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_BURST` and `RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC` env vars). Requests exceeding capacity get a 429 response with `Retry-After` header.

**Request logging**: Every request is logged with a correlation ID (trace ID) — inbound `X-Request-ID` headers are honored, and auto-generated IDs are assigned to requests without one. Sensitive headers (Authorization) and body fields (passwords) are automatically redacted from logs. Each request carries its correlation ID all the way through error responses.

The endpoint also supports sorting (on any allowlisted field like `price`, `category`, `createdAt`) and filtering (category, active status, sku) via query parameters. Invalid sort/filter fields are silently dropped to prevent injection.

All 15 verification checks passed (server boots, pagination walks without duplicates, rate limiting blocks bursts, logging redacts secrets, errors include trace IDs, etc.).

**Design choices made**:
- Cursor-based pagination as the default (no skip/duplicate issues) with offset as an opt-in
- In-memory rate limiter (fine for single instance; note in code to swap for Redis at scale)
- Environment variable configuration for rate limit tuples, falling back to sensible defaults
- Allowlist-based sort/filter fields for security (caller-supplied column names are dropped, never executed)
